solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very soft mini-soap is squishy

indicators.note: something squishy is soft and easily squashed out of shape, so these letters are pushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that some short TV soap opera is soft and squishy.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction meaning very quietly, the softest common marking in a score.

clue.text: Persist in questioning footwear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to question them persistently for information

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for interrogating someone repeatedly and a noun for a plimsoll or dancing shoe.

clue.text: Leave boy enclosing the third of four initial letters

indicators.note: of ties the boy-wrapped letter back to its place among the four initial letters, standing where it was

parts.note: the first four letters of the alphabet

indicators.note: enclosing means the word for boy goes round that third letter

parts.note: a son is a boy
the third of the four initial letters A, B, C, D is C

explanation.surface: A boy flees, taking the third of four initial letters with him.
explanation.walkthrough: The four initial letters are the alphabet's first four; the boy is wrapped round only the third of them, while the other three stay where they are.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to leave secretly, running away to avoid arrest or duty.

clue.text: Irish rise: plebs're somehow immune to subjugation

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: The Irish masses rise up, the common people somehow refusing to be crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irrepressible cannot be held down or restrained by any force.

clue.text: Scene with everything capsized involves unknown danger to shipping

indicators.note: involves means the unknown is taken inside

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for scene in a play script

indicators.note: capsized means turned upside down, so the word for everything runs upward in this down entry

parts.note: all means everything
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A scene where everything has capsized hides some unknown peril to ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Scylla was the rock-dwelling sea monster of Greek myth that seized sailors passing through the strait.

clue.text: Preparation of whites only used by newcomer in guestroom

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hotel provides only white linen for a newcomer staying in the guestroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringue is made from beaten egg whites and sugar, with no yolk at all.

clue.text: Flip charts showing flood with unwanted info

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the word for charts is read backwards

parts.note: charts are maps

explanation.surface: Flip charts in a presentation are said to bury the audience in information they never wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to send masses of junk email or messages to someone.

clue.text: Fantastic beast to goad follower of Sun

parts.note: to poke is to prod or goad
Monday, abbreviated MON, follows Sunday

explanation.surface: A fantastic creature is goaded into following the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pokemon is a fictional creature from the Japanese video game and card franchise.

clue.text: Songs in system arranged with both hands

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a different order, as music is arranged

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, the two hands

explanation.surface: Songs set within a system and arranged for a pianist using both hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Minstrelsy is the art or collected songs of minstrels, the old wandering singers.

clue.text: Liberal in unhappiness but not in spending

indicators.note: in places the letter for Liberal inside the word for unhappiness

parts.note: misery is great unhappiness

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is miserable but refuses to spend money.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserly person is stingy, hoarding money and not taking part in spending.

clue.text: More organised about seizing king, kidnapped again

indicators.note: seizing means holding the letter for king inside
about here means turned round, so the word for more organised runs backwards

parts.note: neater means more organised
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A tidier player turns the game around by capturing the king, like a chess hostage taken back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something retaken has been captured or seized a second time, as a hostage snatched once more.

clue.text: Certain to break handle, wander around Aladdin's cave?

indicators.note: to break means to split the word for handle and sit inside it

parts.note: to treat something is to handle it
sure means certain
to rove is to wander around

explanation.surface: Someone sure to break the handle wanders around a cave of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: In the pantomime tale, Aladdin's cave holds a hoard of hidden riches; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: Whine once undressed, overwhelmed by middle's size

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swallowed up inside the word for middle

parts.note: the core is the middle
to pule is to whine or whimper

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: the word once, used here for its letters

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their middle has grown, the whining once again about their size.
explanation.walkthrough: Undressed works on the printed word once itself, stripping its outer letters, rather than on a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulence is bodily bulk or fatness, a person's large girth.

clue.text: Non-gloss used occasionally for impasto

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of the word impasto is used

explanation.surface: An art tip: a matt paint is only sometimes used for thick impasto work.
explanation.definitionFit: A matte or matt finish is dull rather than shiny, the opposite of a gloss paint.

clue.text: One's written on British poverty before beast died

indicators.note: before puts the poverty ahead of the beast

parts.note: lack is want or poverty
a boar is a wild pig, a beast
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A tale of British poverty before a beast died, as written on a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackboard is the dark surface a teacher writes on with chalk.

clue.text: Paying guest account? Nothing doing for European

indicators.note: doing for means standing in for, so the zero replaces the European letter

parts.note: a ledger is an account book
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A query about a paying guest's bill, which says nothing is being done for a European visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodger rents a room in someone's house, a tenant living with the household.

clue.text: Reportedly modern, from the time of plague

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: new means modern and since means from the time of; spoken together they sound like the answer

explanation.surface: A historian claims some modern outbreak dates from the time of an old plague.
explanation.definitionFit: Here plague is a noun for a pest or annoyance, a thing that troubles someone.

clue.text: Attempt to admit regrets the speaker makes repellent

indicators.note: to admit means to let the regrets inside the attempt

parts.note: a go is an attempt
rues means regrets
the speaker refers to herself or himself as me

explanation.surface: An attempt to admit regrets makes the speaker repellent to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gruesome is horrible and revolting, causing disgust.

clue.text: Strutting of piles beside river

indicators.note: beside puts the river's name right after the piles

parts.note: cocks are piles, as in haycocks, small heaps of hay
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A strutting figure struts past piles of hay beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocksure person is arrogantly confident, just like one swaggering about.

clue.text: Moderate constant urge

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
to hasten is to urge on or hurry

explanation.surface: A cautious voice warns that a constant urge should be moderated.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to restrain or subdue, making someone more moderate.

clue.text: Dangerous point of credit happens more than once

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
happens is IS, and more than once means it appears twice

explanation.surface: A financial warning that credit trouble keeps recurring until it becomes dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a turning point of great danger or difficulty.

clue.text: It brings air to the mouth and not into half of body's frame

definitions.text: It brings air to the mouth

indicators.note: into means the word for and not goes inside
half of keeps only the first half of the word for the body's frame

parts.note: the skeleton is the body's frame
nor means and not

explanation.surface: A device brings air to the mouth and not into the body's frame.
explanation.walkthrough: The body's frame is a synonym that must be found first; only its first half is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A snorkel is a breathing tube that lets a swimmer breathe while face-down in water.

clue.text: What's a person expected to do, cancelling old children's author?

indicators.note: cancelling means the letter for old is struck out

parts.words: What's a person expected to do
parts.note: doing one's bit is doing what one is expected to do

explanation.surface: A question about one's duty, cancelling an old children's writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Nesbit wrote The Railway Children and other well-loved stories for young readers.

clue.text: Utterance frequently addressed to woolgatherers?

parts.note: woolgatherers are daydreamers, but read literally they are sheep, which hear this bleat from one another

explanation.walkthrough: A woolgatherer is an absent-minded daydreamer; taken literally, it is a sheep carrying wool, and sheep call to each other constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the bleating cry of a sheep, the noise a flock makes to its fellows.

clue.text: Not the usual way to get in

definitions.text: Not the usual way to get in

parts.words: Not the usual way to get in
parts.note: a politician normally enters Parliament at a general election; a special vote held between them is another way in

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a side door or back entrance; the getting in is being elected.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-election is held to fill a single vacant seat between general elections, an unusual route into Parliament.

clue.text: Baltic supplier departs dismissed by stranger

indicators.note: dismissed by means the letter for departs is sent out of the word for stranger

parts.note: odder means stranger
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A Baltic trader leaves, dismissed by an odd stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river that flows into the Baltic Sea, supplying it with water.

clue.text: Old-style car towed away, abandoned by wife

indicators.note: away suggests the letters are scattered off elsewhere and put back in a new order
abandoned by means the letter for wife is left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A vintage car is towed off, after a wife has abandoned it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove W from CAR TOWED to leave CAROTED, and rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is a decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s, now a period look.

clue.text: Bore hollow knife in clutch

indicators.note: in places the emptied knife inside the word for clutch

parts.note: a clutch of eggs or chicks is a brood

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its inner letters, keeping only the outside

explanation.surface: Someone bored a hole with a hollow knife held in their grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Here bore is the past tense of bear, to tolerate; brooked means tolerated or allowed.

clue.text: Dip in evacuation site, not to be annoying

indicators.note: not means the word for being annoying is taken away

parts.note: Dunkirk is the French port from which Allied troops were evacuated in 1940
to irk is to annoy

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to dip into an evacuation site without being a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: To dunk is to dip food such as a biscuit into a drink.

clue.text: Top Shop's offering clobber (smaller), with every exchange of small and large

indicators.note: exchange of small and large means the S and L letters trade places in the word for clobber

parts.note: to belt is to clobber, to hit hard
L is the clothing abbreviation for large
S is the clothing abbreviation for small

indicators.note: with every says the same swap is made on each S and L in the word for smaller too

parts.note: lesser means smaller

explanation.surface: A Topshop fashion item is offered in smaller sizes, swapping small and large labels.
explanation.walkthrough: BELT LESSER becomes the answer when every L turns into an S and every S into an L: BELT gives BEST, LESSER gives SELLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop's top-selling item is its bestseller, the product it sells most of.
